add_results.memory: Jeffrey finds religion and becomes a better person, feeling less burdened by guilt and reconnecting with his girlfriend Sarah.
Jeffrey struggles with addiction to online auctions and guilt from cheating on Sarah, feeling lost and alone before discovering a church.
After attending church regularly, Jeffrey finds comfort in messages of forgiveness and redemption, which helps him turn his life around.
Jeffrey makes amends with Sarah and his friends and family, committing to be a better partner and dedicating time to his relationship with Sarah.
As Jeffrey grows and changes, Sarah begins to see the man she fell in love with, leading to a stronger relationship.
The scene concludes with Jeffrey and Sarah sitting in church, holding hands and smiling, having overcome obstacles with the help of Jeffrey's newfound faith.
Jeffrey and Sarah found one last CRT TV that Jeffrey didn't sell online, and they deepen their commitment to each other while playing retro games on it.
Jeffrey and Sarah enjoy reliving childhood memories and sharing nostalgia while playing retro games on the CRT TV, which brings them closer together.
As Jeffrey continues to grow, he realizes he can enjoy both his love for infrared photography and CRT TVs without interfering with his relationship with Sarah.
The scene concludes with Jeffrey and Sarah sitting in front of the CRT TV, holding hands and smiling, having found a way to balance their past and present passions.
Months have passed since Jeffrey's absence from work, prompting Mr. Smith, his boss, to track him down and confront him about the situation.
Mr. Smith expresses concern about Jeffrey's prolonged absence from work, stating it is affecting the company's operations.
Jeffrey explains to Mr. Smith that he has been dealing with personal issues, including an addiction to online auctions and infidelity with his girlfriend.
Mr. Smith acknowledges Jeffrey's personal struggles but emphasizes the impact of his absence on the company, indicating a potential decision to fire him or give him another chance.
Thomas stumbles upon Mr. Smith and Jeffrey during a conversation, mistakenly assuming that Mr. Smith is going to fire Jeffrey due to his personal issues.
Mr. Smith clarifies to Thomas that he is not firing Jeffrey, but rather discussing his recent absence from work.
Thomas feels embarrassed after realizing he jumped to conclusions about Jeffrey's situation and begins to apologize to both Mr. Smith and Jeffrey.
The scene concludes with Thomas reflecting on the importance of being understanding and not judging others based on assumptions, as he contemplates his beautiful photographs in the studio.

Lake Superior is the world's largest freshwater lake by surface area, covering approximately 82,000 square kilometers (31,700 square miles).
Lake Superior is the deepest of the Great Lakes, reaching a maximum depth of 406 meters (1,333 feet).
Lake Superior holds roughly 10% of the world's freshwater supply.
Lake Superior is home to unique plant and animal species, including lake trout, coaster brook trout, and the endangered Piping Plover bird.
Lake Superior is famous for its shipwrecks, with as many as 350 ships having sunk in its waters since the mid-1800s.
User finds the history of shipwrecks on Lake Superior fascinating and inquired about notable shipwrecks in the lake.
The SS Edmund Fitzgerald is one of the most famous shipwrecks on Lake Superior, sinking on November 10, 1975, during a severe storm and taking all 29 crew members with it.
The tragedy of the SS Edmund Fitzgerald was immortalized in the song 'The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald' by Gordon Lightfoot.
Another notable shipwreck on Lake Superior is the SS Cyprus, which sank in 1907 while carrying a cargo of copper during a storm.
It is estimated that as much as 20 million pounds of copper from the SS Cyprus remains on the lake bottom to this day.
Lake Superior has many shipwrecks that attract divers and history buffs due to its unpredictable weather conditions and rocky coastline.
User finds it amazing how much history lies at the bottom of Lake Superior and inquired if people still go diving to explore the shipwrecks.
People still go diving to explore the shipwrecks on Lake Superior, with some wrecks accessible to divers of all levels, while others require specialized equipment and training.
Tour companies offer boat tours of the shipwrecks on Lake Superior, allowing visitors to see the wrecks from above the water, often with researchers and historians as guides.
It is important for divers and visitors to show respect for the shipwrecks on Lake Superior, as many are protected by law and it is illegal to remove artifacts from them.

The Merlion statue stands at 8.6 meters high and weighs 70 tons, located at One Fullerton overlooking Marina Bay, making it one of Singapore's most popular tourist attractions.
The lion's head of the Merlion symbolizes Singapore's Malay name, Singapura, meaning 'lion city', while the fish's body represents its origins as a fishing village.
The Merlion statue reflects Singapore's identity as a maritime nation and has become a beloved symbol featured on stamps, coins, and merchandise.
